title: How high is London's winter Sun?
hook: Everyone knows the winter Sun is lower. Guess how low it gets at noon in London.

knows: that the Sun is lower in winter
that the Earth's axis is tilted
doesNotKnow: how low the winter noon Sun is at a mid-latitude city
that noon height is 90° minus latitude, plus or minus the tilt

misconception: The winter Sun in a mid-latitude city is only a little lower than at the equinox.
objective: The learner can explain that the noon Sun's height is 90° minus latitude plus the Sun's declination, so in London it is about 62° in June, 38° at the equinox and 15° in December: 47° apart, twice the tilt.

claims.text: In London the Sun is about 15° above the horizon at noon on 21 December, 38.5° at the equinox and 61.9° on 21 June.
claims.source: Noon altitude = 90° - latitude + declination (any astronomy text, e.g. Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 13; from memory). Latitude 51.5072°N; declination ±23.44° at the solstices. 15.05°, 38.49°, 61.93° (noonAltitude in Demo.tsx). Geometric: no refraction (adds about 0.1° at 15°; brief). Uses the solstice declination, not the exact value on 21 December of a given year.
51.5072°N, 0.1276°W (gazetteer coordinates for central London; from memory, not checked online).

claims.text: The Earth's axis is tilted about 23.44°, so the noon Sun swings 23.44° above and below its equinox height.
claims.source: Obliquity of the ecliptic 23.44° (Astronomical Almanac; from memory, not checked online). Changes by about 0.013° per century.

claims.text: London's winter noon Sun is about 46.9° lower than its summer noon Sun, twice the tilt.
A low Sun spreads the same light over more ground, and its light passes through more air.
claims.source: Light per unit of level ground scales with sin(altitude): sin 15° / sin 62° = 0.29. Path length through the atmosphere is about 1/sin(altitude) for altitudes above about 10° (plane-parallel air mass), about 3.9 at 15°. Stated qualitatively in the reveal; numbers not shown.

recall.question: A city is at 40°N. Roughly how high is the noon Sun there at the December solstice?
